title: Instagram Giveaways: How to Avoid Collecting Prize Hunters
description: A giveaway can add a thousand followers over a weekend, and nine hundred will be gone within a month. Three rules for running one that leaves you a real audience.
excerpt: A giveaway is the fastest way to gain followers — and the fastest way to kill your reach. The difference is in what you give away.
content:
Giveaways work. You gain 1,200 followers over a weekend and feel like you finally cracked it. Three weeks later your reach is half what it used to be and fewer people see your stories than before the contest. That isn't bad luck — it's arithmetic.

## Why giveaways wreck your reach

Instagram watches the ratio between how many people follow you and how many actually react. When a thousand people arrive wanting an iPhone and then ignore everything else, your engagement rate drops from say 5% to 1.5%. The algorithm draws one conclusion: nobody cares about this content.

You avoid that with a single decision — **what the prize is**.

## Three rules that hold up

**1. Make the prize useless to strangers.** Give away an iPhone and the entire country enters. Give away a year in your course, a kilo of your roasted coffee, or an hour of consulting, and only people it makes sense for will bother. Smaller reach, far better audience.

**2. No mechanics that require tagging fifteen friends.** "Tag 3 friends" manufactures spam, not interest. Ask for a comment answering a question instead — "tell me the part of your training plan you keep skipping." You get ten future post ideas out of the same thread.

**3. Show the draw.** A short video where you pick and announce the winner does two things: it proves the contest was honest, and it earns a second wave of reach. If you'd rather not talk to camera, [TubeVoice](https://tubevoice.io) will put a voiceover over your footage in a couple of minutes.

## The important part comes after

For the first 7 days after the announcement, post content that has nothing to do with the prize. Prize hunters leave on their own, the rest stay. Losing 20–30% is normal and healthy.
